_notes: The guard's only state is a flag file at <tempdir>/ds-workflow-flags/subagent-returned-<CLAUDE_SESSION_ID>,
where <tempdir> is Python's tempfile.gettempdir(). Every case therefore sets TMPDIR='.' so the flag
directory resolves INSIDE the parity sandbox cwd and can be supplied as a fixture. Python's
gettempdir() returns '.' verbatim for TMPDIR='.' (os.curdir is exempted from abspath), so the flag path
is './ds-workflow-flags/subagent-returned-<session>'. A TS port must reproduce that resolution order
(TMPDIR, TEMP, TMP, then the platform default) or the deny branch becomes unreachable and silently allows.
CLAUDE_SESSION_ID is pinned in every case because the harness inherits the real session's value.

cases.name: deny-flag-set-read-of-source-file
cases._tsComment: TS-ONLY EXPECTATION. `sessionFlagKey` now appends a digest of the RAW session id, because deleting disallowed characters was not injective: "sess/one", "sess#one", "sess one", and "sessone" all collapsed to one key, so distinct sessions shared a flag file — the very cross-session leak this key was introduced to stop. Python still names the file after CLAUDE_SESSION_ID verbatim, so the two sides legitimately diverge and the TS side is pinned exactly: stdout hash, exit code, and the full filesystem delta.
